results: Requirement N32 verified: PolicyHelix operates locally without requiring an owned public domain, public DNS or external network connectivity.

Loopback authority boundaries proven: requests to localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] succeed; external and untrusted Host headers (attacker.example.com, evil.invalid, 192.168.1.100) are rejected with HTTP 403 invalid_host, defending against DNS-rebinding attacks.
Cross-origin boundaries proven: requests carrying an external Origin header (attacker.com, malicious.org) targeting API routes are rejected with HTTP 403 invalid_origin.

Cache boundaries proven: dynamic routes (/, /healthz, /readyz, /runtime-config.json, /api/*) strictly emit Cache-Control: no-store; only fingerprinted static assets in /assets/ receive immutable caching.

Optional TLS/private ingress documented in infra/deployment.md and docs/evidence/domain.json, showing Nginx TLS reverse proxying, header stripping (X-Remote-User, X-Forwarded-User) and CIDR whitelisting without exposing engine work by default.
No database schema, migration, .env or Dockerfile was modified; all core features remain open-source Apache-2.0.
observed_limitations: Private hosting behind custom domain names requires explicit operator configuration via allowedHosts or Nginx reverse proxying to maintain DNS-rebinding protection.
coreReady remains false until release gate C30-C40 full sequence is complete; C40 requires maintainer-authorized actual release.
